attacks.claim: The share link embeds the owner's raw project API key as a query parameter in a public URL. Anyone with the link, and any unfurl crawler that fetches it, gets full API access. The share page also returns the key to every viewer as replayKey.
Viewers without an account replay against the owner's project quota. A link posted on HN or X can drain a paid per-token project's budget with no cap, and the owner may not know the link exists.
attacks.evidence: Viewers without an account replay against the owner's project quota.

attacks.claim: Shared conversations are stored publicly with no expiry, access control, or noindex directive, and are server-rendered with Open Graph tags for crawlers. Shared content can persist and spread beyond the owner's control.
attacks.evidence: Share pages are server-rendered with Open Graph tags so links unfurl nicely on Slack/X. / Anyone with the link can view the conversation

attacks.claim: Free signup is email-only with no card, and no verification or abuse control (CAPTCHA, device or IP limits) is described. One actor can create many accounts, multiplying the per-account limits and daily token allowance.
attacks.evidence: Sign up with email, no card required. ABSENT: any abuse or Sybil control for free accounts

attacks.claim: The public promise and the prod config disagree. The changelog promises 20 requests per minute, but the prod config sets 20 per second with burst 40, roughly 1200/min. QA tested the per-minute staging config, so the prod limit was never exercised.
attacks.evidence: Free accounts get **20 requests per minute** ... rate_limit: { requests: 20, per: second, burst: 40 } / staging config used `per: minute`

attacks.claim: Spend is uncapped. max_replicas 24 at $2.49/h is about $43.6k/month at full scale, and nothing enforces the $4k budget. The 100k tokens/day per-account cap across 3,000 accounts allows 300M tokens/day, far above the 126M/month projection. The 2-replica floor alone is about $3.6k, leaving almost no headroom.
attacks.evidence: max_replicas: 24 / within the $4k/month free-tier budget / 100k tokens per day

attacks.claim: The capacity claim is unmeasured. No benchmark or load test supports the under-30% utilization figure, and the projection is a month-1 average, not a launch-hour peak.
attacks.evidence: Two H100 replicas serve the projected free load at < 30% utilization / ABSENT: load test or benchmark of the 8B pool at projected peak

attacks.claim: Launch-day traffic from HN and X at 17:00 UTC will hit a pool held at 2 replicas. Scale-up needs queue depth above 8 sustained for 60s plus GPU provisioning time, so early requests will queue or fail.

Rollback does not stop the harmful effects. Turning off signup leaves existing free keys and autoscaling active, and share links with embedded keys survive rollback. No key revocation or rotation path is described.
attacks.evidence: free_signup_open off stops new signups; existing free keys keep working.

attacks.claim: Alerts cover replica count and error rate only. There is no alert on spend against the $4k budget, on per-account token burn, or on share-link key usage, so a runaway would be seen late or not at all.
attacks.evidence: Alerting: free pool replicas > 6 pages on-call; error rate > 2% pages on-call.

attacks.claim: Deleting a share returns 404 from the app, but cached pages and unfurl caches on third-party platforms may keep showing the content. Deletion also does not revoke the embedded key.
attacks.evidence: Shares can be deleted from Playground → History; deleted shares return 404.

attacks.claim: Both free and paid traffic depend on one GPU provider's on-demand H100 capacity, with no described fallback or portability.
attacks.evidence: at the GPU provider's on-demand rate of $2.49/h

attacks.claim: Publicly shared conversations have no described takedown, erasure, or retention process, which may matter for user data rights and platform terms.
attacks.evidence: Anyone with the link can view the conversation, even without a Lumen account.

attacks.claim: The Share action gives no warning that the link also grants access to the owner's API key and billing.
attacks.evidence: Click 'Share' on any playground session to get a link.

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-blocking found in the rendering or layout described.
attacks.evidence: Share pages are server-rendered with Open Graph tags so links unfurl nicely on Slack/X.

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-blocking found; the artifact does not describe the share or signup flows' accessibility, so this is unverified rather than cleared.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: accessibility QA for signup and share flows

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-blocking found in the signup-to-first-request path, which QA measured under 60s.
attacks.evidence: Signup → first free request in < 60s: pass.

attacks.claim: Gateway logs are reduced to metadata, but the share store keeps full message content, which the logging section does not cover.
attacks.evidence: we log model, token counts, latency, status and project id only
